ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

gustilo — pattern 4

A patient has a contaminated open tibial fracture after an industrial crush injury. Debridement reveals periosteal stripping and exposed bone that cannot be covered by the remaining local tissue. A flap is needed, but the limb artery is intact. Which Gustilo–Anderson grade best describes the injury?

  1. Type IIIB
  2. Type IIIC
  3. Type I
  4. Type II
  5. Type IIIA
Answer and explanation

Type IIIB

Type IIIB: An open fracture with extensive soft-tissue loss, periosteal stripping and inadequate bone coverage requiring flap reconstruction.

Option explanations

Type IIIB: Type IIIB: An open fracture with extensive soft-tissue loss, periosteal stripping and inadequate bone coverage requiring flap reconstruction.

Type IIIC: Type IIIC describes an open fracture associated with an arterial injury requiring repair, regardless of wound size. The case instead matches Type IIIB.

Type I: Type I describes a low-energy open fracture with a clean wound under 1 cm and minimal soft-tissue damage. The case instead matches Type IIIB.

Type II: Type II describes an open fracture with a wound over 1 cm but without extensive soft-tissue destruction, flaps or avulsion. The case instead matches Type IIIB.

Type IIIA: Type IIIA describes a severe open fracture with adequate viable soft-tissue coverage of the bone. The case instead matches Type IIIB.
